# Whatfix — AI & Agent Framing (2025–2026)

## What it is
**Whatfix** — an enterprise Digital Adoption Platform (DAP) that overlays in-app guidance, training simulations, and analytics onto other software so employees adopt new systems. In 2025-2026 it repositioned as **"AI-Powered Digital Adoption Platform."** URL: https://whatfix.com

---

## Verbatim taglines & hero copy

**Homepage:**
- "Increase user adoption with in-app guidance"
- "In-app guidance. Hands-on simulations. Actionable analytics. One unified platform to drive adoption and maximize ROI."
- "Software Clicks Better With Whatfix"

**AI Adoption solution page** (https://whatfix.com/solutions/ai-adoption/):
- "Whatfix for AI Adoption"
- "Accelerating AI Value in the Flow of Work"
- "AI Adoption Clicks Better With Whatfix"
- "Deploying AI ≠ Using AI"
- "Investing in AI is just the first step. Without adoption, efficiency gains remain theoretical"
- "Employees who are early AI adopters have 40% higher-quality output"

---

## ScreenSense — the core AI engine (launched Feb 27, 2025)
URL: https://whatfix.com/ai/screensense/

- "Introducing ScreenSense"
- "ScreenSense™ is Whatfix's patented context & intent engine that perceives user interfaces like humans"
- **Hero tagline:** "Helping your software understand users — so your users don't need to understand your software."
- "ScreenSense brings intelligence to every screen by recognizing what users are doing, understanding what they need, and responding in the moment"
- Three-pillar frame — **Context:** "identifies the screen your user is on and what they're interacting with"; **Intent:** "interprets their behavior and pinpoints their intent"; **Action:** "triggers the right in-app guidance, help article, or automation — instantly"
- "Real-time, intuitive assistance that adapts to their needs" / "Contextual, personalized guidance that simplifies complex tasks" / "support users in the flow of work"

**"Userization" is their signature strategic word.** CEO Khadim Batti: "Whatfix AI Agents flip that equation. They **userize** technology to adapt to the user's context." "At the heart of the userization approach is ScreenSense."

---

## Whatfix AI Agents (launched Sept 2025)
URL: https://whatfix.com/newsroom/press-releases/whatfix-launches-ai-agents-to-accelerate-business-outcomes-for-enterprises/

A "unified suite of AI Agents … a native intelligence layer embedded across the Whatfix suite," all powered by ScreenSense, which "continuously interprets both the users' context within an application and the user's real-time intent."

- **Guidance Agent** — "delivers precise, AI-generated answers **in the flow of work**, distilling complex or lengthy knowledge into short, contextual summaries" — so users get clarity "without switching tabs, reading long documents, or escalating."
- **Authoring Agent** — generates "fully configured in-app experiences using simple natural language."
- **Insights Agent** — "ask questions in natural language to uncover user behavior and drop-off patterns."

Executive framing:
- Batti: "This is not just about improving adoption. It is about enabling **every user** to succeed."
- Customer (Servier, Operational Excellence Director): "With Whatfix AI, we're heading towards a world where digital solutions will self-correct, self-improve, and **personalize in real time**."

---

## The STORY FRAME — how they narrate walking an employee through change
From the change-management page (https://whatfix.com/change-management/), verbatim:
- "Enterprise software change management is the discipline of **preparing users, guiding them through changed workflows, and measuring whether the change improves execution once it goes live.**"
- "Strong teams use it to **prepare users before launch, support them in the flow of work after go-live, and improve the workflow as real behavior reveals friction points.**"

The AI-adoption arc is narrated as an awareness-to-value lifecycle: "Empower end-users across the technology adoption lifecycle, from awareness to value" → "drive awareness of new AI capabilities" → "Surface contextual use cases at key moments, nudge users to experiment" → "Support users when they experience frustration" → "Guide users in the flow of work and provide AI assistance" → "Train users with hands-on simulations and AI roleplay in a risk-free sandbox."

Note the frame is **system-centric, not person-centric**: the software adapts to the user ("userize"), rather than a persistent companion accompanying a named individual.

---

## Emotional / strategic angle
- **Fear of wasted investment / ROI anxiety:** "Deploying AI ≠ Using AI"; "efficiency gains remain theoretical" without adoption. A commissioned study headline: enterprises "Stand to Lose $10.9M Annually Due to Poor Digital Adoption."
- **Relief from complexity:** "so your users don't need to understand your software" — remove the burden of learning from the human.
- **Inevitability / future-facing:** "self-correct, self-improve, and personalize in real time."

---

## Who the buyer is
Whatfix targets **operational/IT/enablement owners, not primarily the CHRO or a "Head of Change" title.** Verbatim role-targeting language:
- "Enterprise Application Owner," "Transformation Program Lead," "IT leaders and application owners," "Business process owners," "Regional leaders," plus "L&D" and "Service desk teams."
- "For **IT leaders and application owners**, its value is practical: reduce disruption, protect process quality, contain support demand, and shorten the time it takes users to become competent on new or updated systems."
- Solution pages also address L&D, HR, Product Teams, and digital-transformation leaders (implied CIO/CHRO/Head of Enablement), but the *named* personas skew toward **app owners, transformation leads, and IT** — the people accountable for a rollout — not an HR change persona.

---

## CRITICAL question: a personal 1:1 AI companion walking each individual through a change?

**No — Whatfix does not frame a personal 1:1 AI companion.** This is the key differentiator for your positioning:

- Their agents are an **"embedded intelligence layer"** and **"AI Agents"** scoped to functions (Guidance, Authoring, Insights) — tools that serve *whoever* is on a screen, not a persistent companion assigned to a named employee.
- The framing is **software-adapts-to-user ("userize")**, in-the-moment and stateless: "recognizing what users are doing … responding in the moment," "adapts to their needs." It's contextual assistance triggered by screen + intent, not an ongoing relationship.
- The AI-in-DAP blog explicitly frames the agents as **execution-acceleration/information-delivery tools where "humans retain accountability"** — "There is no explicit mention of personalized individual companions or agentic systems operating independently for single employees during change adoption."
- Closest they get: the Guidance Agent surfaces "the right information at the exact moment of need by reading underlying application workflows and user intent" — but that's contextual info delivery inside a workflow, **not a 1:1 companion that accompanies a person through their whole adoption journey.**

The words "personalized," "real-time intent," and "in the flow of work" are everywhere, but "personalized" means *the response is tailored to the current screen/context*, not *a dedicated agent that is yours over time*. There is no "your AI companion," no per-employee persistent agent, no 1:1 relationship framing. That white space is theirs to lose and yours to claim.

# Pendo — Adoption / Guidance & Employee-App ("Adopt") Research (2025-2026)

## What it is
**Pendo** — a product-experience and digital adoption platform (DAP) combining product analytics, in-app guidance, feedback, and (2025-2026) AI agent analytics + agentic assistants. Two arms: **customer-facing** (SaaS products) and **employee-facing / "Pendo for your employees" / Pendo Adopt** (internal workplace software adoption). URL: https://www.pendo.io

---

## VERBATIM taglines & hero copy

**Homepage** (https://www.pendo.io):
- Hero: *"Close the gap between AI spend and AI adoption."*
- *"Meet Novus — the agent that manages your product for you"*
- *"Pendo captures user behavior across your software and agents, identifies where users struggle, and puts that context to work"*
- *"Everything you need to understand users and drive adoption—for products and agents."*
- *"Give your AI agents the context they need"*

**Pendo AI page** (https://www.pendo.io/ai/):
- Hero: *"A new way to build products."*
- *"Focus on the work only you can do with cutting-edge AI, from your always-on assistant to predictive LLMs."*
- Novus: *"Meet Novus — the agent that manages your product for you"*
- Leo: *"Use a conversational AI interface to generate insights, automate tasks, and take action."*
- *"Create guides in minutes, not hours."* (AI Guide Creation)

**Employee-facing page** (https://www.pendo.io/pendo-for-your-employees/):
- Hero: *"Power the digital workplace experience"*
- *"Get more from your tech investments with the only intelligent digital adoption platform"*
- *"One product suite. Infinite business value."*
- *"Accelerate user proficiency and keep employees in flow"*
- *"Guide employees through change and standardize workflows"*
- *"Contextual guidance, when and where they need it"*
- *"Segment users for personalized guidance"*

**In-App Guides** (https://www.pendo.io/product/in-app-guides/):
- Hero: *"In-app Guides: Help customers get more from your apps and agents"*
- Tagline: *"Personalized in-app guidance, right where users need it."*
- *"Guide users to high-value features with embedded guides, walkthroughs, and tooltips that surface only when needed."*
- *"Personalize every experience: Segment and target guides to reach the right users, at the right time, with the right message."*

**Agent Analytics** (https://www.pendo.io/product/agent-analytics/):
- Hero: *"Measure and scale AI agents."*
- *"Agents are changing how you use software."*
- *"See users work across agents and apps."*
- *"Pendo Agent Analytics monitors both agents you build and third-party agents your employees use—including ChatGPT, Claude, GitHub Copilot."*

---

## The STORY FRAME — how they narrate walking an employee through change

Pendo's narrative is **change-management-at-scale**, not a personal hand-holding companion. It's framed as an org planning and standardizing change, informed by behavioral data. Verbatim from the **Change Management page** (https://www.pendo.io/digital-adoption/change-management/):

- Hero: *"Change management at scale"*
- *"Transition employees to new and better ways of working with Pendo's intelligent digital adoption platform."*
- *"See how work happens now"* → *"Get AI-powered insights on how your employees work today so you can plan the right change for tomorrow."*
- *"Establish best practices"* → *"Create consistency and predictability in how you manage change in your organization."*
- *"Learn from your star employees"* → *"Identify and leverage super users as change champions to inform your support and guidance strategy."*

The employee-side story (from employee-productivity page): *"Shorten ramp time with personalized onboarding to help employees understand cross-app processes"* and *"Support employees with contextual guidance, when and where they need it."*

**Key distinction:** the "walking through" happens via **in-app guides, walkthroughs, tooltips, and Guide Branching** — content the org authors and targets — not a conversational agent that accompanies each person. Guide Branching (Autumn 2025) is the closest to individualization: *"Create dynamic in-app experiences that adapt to each user's choices. With conditional logic built into your guides, you can deliver tailored content and next steps that match individual needs."*

---

## Emotional / strategic angle
- **Rational/ROI-led, not emotional.** The 2025-2026 wrapper is the **AI adoption ROI gap**: *"Close the gap between AI spend and AI adoption."* / *"Track AI, prove ROI."*
- Employee side leans on **flow and proficiency** (*"keep employees in flow,"* *"accelerate proficiency"*) — productivity framing, not empowerment/growth.
- **Data-first change:** change should be *"data-informed"* and *"predictable,"* leveraging *"super users as change champions."* Top-down, org-orchestrated — the buyer plans change; employees receive it.

---

## WHO the buyer is
Pendo **does not name CHRO / Head of Change / Head of Enablement** in hero copy. Role-targeting is soft and org-level (*"your employees," "your team," "your organization"*). The one page with explicit personas is **Agent Analytics**, which lists:
- *"Agent builders — Increase revenue, cut costs, reduce risk"*
- *"Product teams — Optimize adoption and identify friction"*
- *"IT organizations — Track employee-facing agent usage across portfolios"*
- *"Revenue teams — Monitor adoption gaps and churn signals"*

So the real buyer skews **Product teams and IT/CIO org** (plus agent builders), with employee-experience/change practitioners addressed only implicitly. HR/CHRO is notably absent from the copy.

---

## AI / "companion" / "1:1" / "in the flow of work" language (verbatim)
- *"your always-on assistant"* (Pendo AI)
- *"Meet Novus — the agent that manages your product for you"* (Novus is the agent — it manages the **product for the builder**, not an employee's onboarding)
- **Leo** — *"Pendo's conversational interface,"* used to *"generate insights, automate tasks, and take action"* and to *"create guides and steps"* (Leo builds guides; it is not the employee's personal guide-through-change)
- Autumn 2025 release: *"A new agent-first Pendo experience,"* *"Agent Mode is: Conversational, Proactive, Always on,"* *"your new intelligent AI agent that can perform autonomous tasks on your behalf,"* *"Personalized paths to guide every user to success,"* *"deeper personalization, smoother journeys."*
- Employee page: *"keep employees in flow"* and *"contextual guidance, when and where they need it"* (the "in the flow of work" idea, expressed as in-app guidance rather than an AI companion).

Note: there is **no explicit "AI companion" or "1:1"** phrasing on Pendo's own pages. The Autumn 2025 release page specifically did **not** use "companion" or "1:1" language.

---

## Do they frame a PERSONAL 1:1 AI companion that walks each individual employee through adopting a change?

**No — not for employees.** This is the key strategic gap. Pendo's AI agents point in two directions, neither of which is a personal per-employee change-adoption companion:

1. **Novus / Leo** are aimed at the **product manager / builder** ("the agent that manages your product for you," a conversational interface to build guides and analyze data). The AI works **for the operator**, not alongside the individual employee.
2. **Agent Analytics** is about **measuring** agents ("Measure and scale AI agents," tracking employees' use of ChatGPT/Claude/Copilot) — observation, not companionship.

The employee actually experiencing a change gets **authored, targeted in-app guides** (segmented, branchable) — *"Personalized in-app guidance, right where users need it"* — which is rules-based personalization (segment + conditional logic), not a conversational 1:1 AI that walks each person through their adoption. The closest they come is Guide Branching's *"next steps that match individual needs"* and *"Personalized paths to guide every user to success"* — but these are pre-built decision trees, not an individual AI companion.

**Whitespace for NanoCo/Shellano:** Pendo owns *measuring* adoption and *authoring* org-level guidance, and it frames AI as a tool for the product/IT operator. It does **not** offer each employee a personal AI that lives beside them and walks them through a change conversationally, in their own words, in the flow of work. That personal-companion-per-employee framing is exactly the space Pendo's copy leaves open.
